Method of Attack: Deployed via Windows 10 App Installer using malicious .appinstaller and .appxbundle files
Delivered as a fake Adobe PDF Component AppX app bundle
Phishing spam campaign impersonating company manager with threatening language
Malware harvests system information and sends it to command-and-control server disguised as HTTPS cookies
Injection of malicious code into headless Chromium-based Edge browser process
Used to deliver additional payloads such as Cobalt Strike beacons and Ryuk ransomware
Attack Vector: Highly targeted spam phishing emails with links to fake PDF download pages hosted on Microsoft cloud storage (*.web.core.windows.net)
Use of ms-appinstaller: protocol to launch Windows App Installer
Malicious files hosted on Microsoft cloud storage domains and adobeview subdomains
Indicators of Compromise: Malicious .appinstaller and .appxbundle files hosted on Microsoft cloud storage root directories
Payload named Security.exe nested within UpdateFix subfolder
Command-and-control server communications disguised as HTTPS GET or POST cookies
SophosLabs Github page with IoCs including malware sample hashes, C2 server URLs, and source URLs
